sections.title: Molecular profile of uterine carcinosarcoma
sections.intro: Carcinosarcoma is, molecularly, a serous-like p53-aberrant carcinoma with extreme copy-number instability. **Median ploidy 3.3, with ≥1 whole-genome doubling in 90% of tumours — the highest of any TCGA tumour type** (vs 54% in high-grade serous ovarian, P<0.001) [1]. By mutation signature, 43/55 classifiable TCGA cases (78%) were serous-like and 12 (22%) endometrioid-like; all 10 stage IV cases were serous-like [1].

cells: TP53 mutated in **all but 5 of 57 (91%)** [1]; TP53 86% in a 168-case commercial panel [15]; **37/37 (100%)** in a population-based series [8]; CNH 64/109 (59%) by genomic subtype [2]
**1.8% (1/57)** TCGA [1] vs **10.1% (11/109)** in the Japanese JFCR cohort [2]
~**3.6%** on re-analysis of TCGA; **10/109 (9.2%)** CNL in JFCR [2]

*~13–23%, depending on scoring criteria* (13/80, 16% by 2013 breast criteria vs 10/80, 13% by 2007 [17]; 7/48, 15% by CISH [19]; 10/44, 23% by FISH in a selected cohort [18]); *ERBB2 amplified 9%* [15]

notes.title: The non-p53abn minority is small but treatment-relevant — do not report a single number
notes.md: **MMRd and POLE rates differ ~5-fold between North American and Japanese cohorts** (MMRd 3.5–6% vs 22%; POLE 1.8% vs 10.1%) [1,2,10,11,15]. Gotoh attributes this to the carcinoma component — 85.0% of JFCR uterine CS had an **endometrioid** component vs 81.3% serous/undifferentiated in TCGA UCS — and raises ethnic/cohort differences [2]. MMRd carcinosarcomas are usually p53 wild-type (7/10 tested at MSKCC [10]; 4/4 in [11]), and all molecular classes occur in tumours with sarcomatous components [12]. For a Taiwanese practice the Japanese distribution may be the more relevant prior, which raises the expected yield of MMR testing. **An MMRd or POLEmut result should be acted on as a treatment modifier**, like the same class in any other endometrial carcinoma.

notes.title: Practical consequence for testing
notes.md: Molecular classification does **not** stratify treatment within carcinosarcoma the way it does in endometrioid carcinoma — almost every case lands in p53abn. Its value in UCS is (a) **MMR status as a treatment modifier** for chemo-immunotherapy, (b) **POLEmut** as the rare class with no recurrences in pooled data [13], and (c) **p53-aberrancy as the trigger for HER2 testing**: ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 recommends HER2 testing in all advanced/recurrent p53abn endometrial carcinomas and in serous carcinomas and carcinosarcomas [74]. For HER2-directed therapy, the IHC score and ISH result are not interchangeable in UCS: heterogeneity is common, and amplification was found in only 50% of IHC 3+ tumours in one 148-case series [17,18,20]. Because STATICE showed responses down to IHC 1+ (§3B), T-DXd eligibility is an IHC question, not an amplification question.

notes.title: The adjuvant standard rests on a non-significant trial plus a non-inferiority trial
notes.md: **GOG-150 did not reach significance on either endpoint.** Chemotherapy displaced whole-abdominal irradiation as the adjuvant backbone on a *trend* (death RH 0.712, P=.085) [36]. **GOG-0261 then established carboplatin/paclitaxel by non-inferiority against paclitaxel/ifosfamide, not by superiority over anything** [37] — its PFS *was* significantly superior to ifosfamide/paclitaxel, but ifosfamide/paclitaxel is the comparator, not observation. Do not read "37 vs 29 months" as the benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy. **GOG-0261 is 46% stage I–II and 8% recurrent.** It is simultaneously the adjuvant trial, the advanced-disease trial and part of the first-line-for-recurrence trial in this disease, which is why it is duplicated into Tables 2 and 3A. Never split its numbers across tables. ⚠️ A widely cited review characterises GOG-261's PFS benefit as concentrated "particularly in stages III–IV" [16]. **The full text does not support "particularly":** the stage III–IV subgroup had PFS HR 0.65 (0.48–0.88) and OS HR 0.74 (0.54–1.01, NS), but there was no statistically significant heterogeneity across subgroups [37]. Do not assert a stage-concentrated benefit. ⚠️ Toxicity in GOG-0261 is reported only qualitatively in the abstract: similar overall, with **more haematologic toxicity on carbo/paclitaxel** and **more confusion and genitourinary haemorrhage on paclitaxel/ifosfamide**. Full text (Table 2, treated UCS, PC vs PI): grade 3–4 haematologic **82% vs 50%** (P<.01); neurologic 7% vs 11%; haemorrhage 0% vs 1%.

notes.title: PORTEC-3 is not carcinosarcoma evidence — and its PDFs are currently ambiguous in this vault
notes.md: Carcinosarcoma was never eligible for PORTEC-3 [41]; the p53abn post-hoc analysis that EMCA_Serous_Algorithm_v1.2 uses as a serous proxy therefore **cannot** be used as a carcinosarcoma proxy, even though UCS is ~90% p53abn. The row is retained deliberately: a marked-excluded row is more informative than an absent one. `GO_PDFs/` currently holds six PORTEC-3 PDFs (`2016_deBoer_The Lancet Oncology.pdf`, `2018_deBoer_The Lancet Oncology.pdf`, `2019_deBoer_The Lancet Oncology.pdf`, `2020_León-Castillo_Journal of Clinical Oncology.pdf`, `2021_Post_International Journal of Radiation Oncology Biology Physics.pdf`, `2025_Post_The Lancet Oncology.pdf`) with matching `GO_summaries/` extracts. **The file↔paper mapping was verified on 2026-09-19** by reading page 1 of each PDF and matching the printed title, authors and journal citation line — all six map correctly, and there is a single 2018 file (no `_dup` copy exists). See Open items.

notes.title: There is no "low-risk" carcinosarcoma
notes.md: 97 cases of carcinosarcoma **without myometrial invasion** (FIGO 2009 IA; FIGO 2023 IC), 11 centres: tumour confined to a polyp in 28.9%, confined to endometrium in 56.7%, and **no residual disease in the hysterectomy specimen in 14.4%**. Outcome: **29.9% recurred, mostly distant; 5-yr RFS 63.5% (53.4–75.4); 5-yr OS 72.0% (62.6–82.9)**. No significant difference in RFS or OS by tumour status (P=.99, P=.43) — including the 14 with no residual tumour at all. Receipt of chemotherapy: **RFS P=.08, OS P=.07 — not statistically significant** [35]. Read both halves. Even a carcinosarcoma with zero myoinvasion carries ~30% recurrence and ~28% 5-year mortality, which is the strongest argument against observing any UCS. And simultaneously: **no study has ever demonstrated a statistically significant chemotherapy benefit in this subgroup.** Both facts belong in the consent conversation. In practice ~40% of US patients receive no adjuvant therapy at all — 42.0% of 5614 stage I cases [29], 40.5% of 4272 stage I–III cases (70.8% no chemotherapy) [46], 39.9% of 10,609 all-stage cases [47]. That reflects under-treatment and selection, not evidence of safety.

sections.title: 1B. Adjuvant radiotherapy — retrospective evidence only
sections.intro: There is **no randomized trial of adjuvant RT vs observation in UCS, and none of adjuvant chemotherapy ± RT in UCS.** GOG-150 is the only RCT with an RT arm and it had no no-RT control [36]. This is the single largest evidence gap in the disease, so the retrospective series are admitted here (*italicised*, as in EMCA_ClearCell_Algorithm_v1.2), each uncontrolled and pre-molecular.

notes.title: ⭐ The one place radiotherapy in UCS has a defensible indication
notes.md: 443 **stage I** UCS from a 26-institution cohort. On multivariate analysis **chemotherapy — but not radiotherapy — independently reduced both local (adj-HR 0.46, 0.25–0.83, P=.01) and distant recurrence (adj-HR 0.41, 0.27–0.62, P<0.001)**. Chemo+RT vs chemo alone overall: local recurrence 5.1% vs 10.1%, adj-HR 0.46 (0.13–1.58), **P=.22, NS**. **But there is an interaction.** Radiotherapy significantly decreased local recurrence when tumours had high-grade carcinoma, **sarcoma-component dominance**, or deep myometrial invasion (all P<.05); and adding RT to chemotherapy reduced local recurrence versus chemotherapy alone **only in the presence of multiple risk factors — 5-yr cumulative local recurrence 2.5% vs 21.8%, HR 0.12 (0.02–0.90), P=.013 — and not with none or one factor (P=.36)** [42]. This reconciles the whole literature: RT does not improve survival on average (OS [28]; PFS on multivariate analysis [23]), because most recurrences are distant (5-yr distant 28.1% vs local 13.3% [42]) and fall outside the field; but in **sarcoma-dominant, high-grade, deeply invasive stage I** disease the loco-regional modality earns its place — consistent with the finding that sarcoma components spread loco-regionally while carcinoma components spread lymphatically [23]. Retrospective and subgroup-derived, but biologically coherent. **Sarcoma dominance is therefore a pathology field worth asking for explicitly.**

notes.title: One registry result to flag and not repeat
notes.md: SARCUT reports adjuvant chemotherapy associated with **worse** DFS (HR 1.84, 1.27–2.67) [34]. This is almost certainly confounding by indication — sicker, higher-burden patients received chemotherapy — and it contradicts GOG-0261 and every Matsuo analysis. **Do not report it as a treatment effect.**

notes.title: ⭐ The single most clinically actionable point in this note
notes.md: **The three positive first-line chemo-immunotherapy trials are not interchangeable for carcinosarcoma.** RUBY, DUO-E and AtTEnd enrolled carcinosarcoma; **NRG-GY018 excluded it.** Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy therefore has no carcinosarcoma evidence from its pivotal trial, whereas dostarlimab (RUBY) and durvalumab (DUO-E, dMMR) do. → **For carcinosarcoma the carried chemo-IO option is dostarlimab + carbo/paclitaxel (and durvalumab + carbo/paclitaxel if dMMR) — not pembrolizumab + carbo/paclitaxel.** This is the easiest error to make at the bedside, because the four regimens are otherwise near-identical. Second caution: **"eligible" is not "shown to work".** RUBY, DUO-E and AtTEnd all published carcinosarcoma counts, but only AtTEnd published a carcinosarcoma efficacy estimate — an unplanned PFS subgroup of 50 patients, HR 0.88 (0.45–1.73), uninformative. Otherwise the trial-wide HRs are all that exists, and they are not carcinosarcoma HRs.

notes.title: Reading the historical GOG rows
notes.md:
- **GOG-108's P values are one-tailed** and the authors' own conclusion was that the PFS gain was "small" and "the added toxicity may not justify the use of this combination" — grade 3–4 granulocytopenia 60% vs 36%, and treatment may have contributed to 6 deaths on full-dose 5-day ifosfamide/cisplatin [38].
- **GOG-161 is the only UCS trial ever to show a significant OS gain** (13.5 vs 8.4 mo, HR 0.69) [39]. Ifosfamide/paclitaxel was therefore the regimen "with established superiority" that GOG-0261 had to match — which is why GOG-0261 was designed as non-inferiority, and why its 37-month median OS in a 46%-early-stage population is not comparable to GOG-161's 13.5 months in measurable advanced/recurrent disease.
- **Outcomes have not moved in four decades.** 5-yr OS 31.9% (1975) → 33.8% (2012); incidence rising (APC 2000–2016 1.7%, 95% CI 1.2–2.2); UCS now >5% of endometrial cancer. Across 26 trials in recurrent/metastatic UCS, median RR 37.5% and median PFS 5.9 mo after first line, falling to **5.5% and 1.8 mo** in later lines [16].

sections.title: 3. Recurrent disease
sections.intro: Recurrent disease is **not one setting**. The GOG carcinosarcoma trials treated recurrence with first-line cytotoxic therapy in patients who had never had chemotherapy; the modern trials treat recurrence after platinum and, increasingly, after a checkpoint inhibitor. Table 3 is therefore split by **line of therapy**, not by "recurrent" as a label.

notes.title: Why this split exists, and why it bites harder in carcinosarcoma
notes.md: GOG-108 and GOG-232B **excluded prior cytotoxic chemotherapy**; GOG-0261 enrolled chemo-naive patients, 8% of whom were recurrent. Their recurrent patients received a platinum or ifosfamide doublet as their *first* systemic therapy. Reading GOG-0261's 37-month median OS as a salvage-line expectation would be a large error — GOG-161's 13.5 months in measurable advanced/recurrent disease is the closer comparator, and later-line medians are ~1.8 months of PFS [16]. **The carcinosarcoma-specific problem is worse than for serous.** In EMCA_Serous_Algorithm_v1.2 the 3B rows are all-histology trials with a serous stratum. Here, most of the 3B rows are trials that **excluded carcinosarcoma outright**. Every registrational second-line regimen in endometrial cancer — lenvatinib/pembrolizumab, dostarlimab monotherapy, pembrolizumab monotherapy — was developed in a population that barred this histology, while the approvals themselves do not specify histologic subtype [73]. Label-level use in UCS is extrapolation across an exclusion criterion, which is a different and weaker thing than extrapolation across an unreported subgroup.

notes.title: Reading notes for 3B
notes.md:
- **T-DXd is the one place carcinosarcoma has better evidence than most histotypes.** STATICE is a dedicated UCS trial, and it is positive at a threshold **lower** than for serous: responses occurred at IHC 1+ (ORR 70%, n=10). The HER2-low cohort is n=10 — a wide confidence interval (34.8–93.3), not a precise 70%. Preclinical bystander-killing data in UCS lines support activity independent of uniform HER2 expression.
- **The 27% ILD rate is the number to quote in consent**, not the 10–15% pooled T-DXd figure — and note it was not independently adjudicated, and was 36% at the 6.4 mg/kg dose versus 21% at the 5.4 mg/kg dose now used [56].
- **TROP2 is a real target with a disappointing carcinosarcoma result so far.** TROP2 is detectable in ≥90% of archival UCS and UCS organoids/PDX respond to sacituzumab govitecan [68] — yet the clinical CS stratum gave 1/11 responses, with lower TROP2 protein in CS than in serous [61]. TroFuse-005 (sac-TMT, CS eligible, both primary endpoints met) is the readout that matters; it is currently **press-release only**.
- **Three of the six "standard" salvage options in this table explicitly barred carcinosarcoma** (KEYNOTE-775, GARNET, TROPiCS-03), and ADAGIO and GOG-0086P did too. This is the boundary clinicians cross without noticing, because the approvals are histology-agnostic while the trials were not.
- Hormonal options are omitted, as in EMCA_Serous_Algorithm_v1.2: UCS is typically ER/PR-low and there is no carcinosarcoma-specific evidence.
